newsitem.title: USA: U.S. gold mines profits boosted by hedging - report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. gold mines profits boosted by hedging - report.

text.p: Over 10 percent of the U.S. gold mining industry's profits were earned by the use of hedging techniques in 1995, the U.S. Gold Institute said in a report issued Monday.
"This makes hedging an important element of precious metals producers' performance," the author of the report, John Dobra said.
Dobra, from the Natural Resource Institute at the University of Nevada, prepared the biennial report on the U.S. gold industry for the U.S. Gold Institute.
Over the past three years, U.S. producers have mainly used forward sales contracts, spot deferred contracts and put and call options as risk management and revenue enhancement devices, Dobra said.
By contrast, since gold prices reached inflation-adjusted lows in the early 1980s, gold loans, which were popular in the late 1980s, have all but ceased to exist, he said.
At the end of 1995, a total of 18.3 million ounces of worldwide production by North American producers was sold forward, the report said.
As of the end of 1995, worldwide 1996 gold production by North American producers, was 42 percent hedged at $408 an ounce, while 29 percent of 1997 production was hedged at $421 an ounce.
About eight percent of 1998 output was hedged at $447 an ounce, eight percent of 1999 production was hedged at $467 an ounce, and seven percent of 2000 production was hedged at $435 an ounce.
Spot gold prices at the end of 1995 were around $386 an ounce and currently are around $340 an ounce.
"Our survey of major US producers showed about 10 ounces of gold sold via spot deferred contracts for every one ounce sold via fixed forward contracts," Dobra said.
"A broader survey conducted by Scotia McLeod in 1996 however shows a ratio of approximately two ounces sold via spot deferred contracts for every one sold via fixed forwards," he said.

Spot deferred contracts are a commitment to sell gold at a future date at the current spot price, but the seller may elect to defer delivery if the spot price at the agreed upon delivery date is higher than the spot price agreed on in the contract.
"Because of this flexibility to sell at the higher of two prices, spot deferred contracts are used much more frequently than fixed forward sales," he said.
Forward sales contracts are commitments to sell gold at a future date at a predetermined price, usually with a bullion bank as the counter-party.
